# Independent audit of joint row funding and tetrahedral incidence

Source: `candidate 58f8bbb67f63ee23` (Sections 1–4).



The direct sum of the selected positive Hessian subspaces maps to the quotient by the active-row span. A nonzero kernel tuple can be funded by exact row scalings. Full positivity is needed only for the selected perturbations; all other rows preserve their supports. The exact homogeneous projective identity shows that all scaling cross terms cancel. Thus the joint bound k+sum p_i<=m is valid and is stronger than requiring an individual direction to lie in the active span.

The completed-square Schur formula agrees with the independently differentiated blocks in `candidate a5d3d44181ebed82`. Its correcting map is injective on the g-orthogonal subspace and preserves collective funding modulo the active-row span because that span contains 1.

In the one-hole k=3 calculation, the sum of the two full-row margins at the missing column is exactly -t_z<0. Weak exclusion of the hole suffices to leave both strictly captured vertices central. The remaining case—one noncentral hole captured by precisely one full row—is correctly retained rather than dismissed by a one-direction count.

The tetrahedral quadrilateral opposite-side inequalities multiply to an impossible strict inequality. The triangular and through-vertex section centroids have the stated at-most-1/3 bounds on their captured coordinates, with a boundary vertex coordinate exactly 1/3. The Section 4 full-rank case split therefore checks. A one-zero row can permit only its missing coordinate to be noncentral; repeated holes are correctly removable at a minimal-active maximum because their rows are proportional with equal objective weights.

The newer all-dimensional density-tangent same-side lemma in the Schur source replaces the special tetrahedral opposite-side calculation and makes the same full-rank sign argument available in every dimension. That extension does not by itself remove lower-rank multiple-full-row configurations.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
